title: BASIC let beginners share a computer through terminals
body: John Kemeny and Thomas Kurtz launched Dartmouth's time-sharing system in 1964. Students could type and run programs in BASIC at terminals, with the same central computer giving different users turns.
takeaway: Quick feedback makes it easier to try an idea than submitting a batch job and waiting for the result.
source: Computer History Museum, Dartmouth Professors Launch Timesharing System (1964)
visual: several early typing terminals along one classroom wall

title: The original Apple computer was sold as a board
body: The Apple-1 debuted in 1976. For 666.66 US dollars, buyers received a populated circuit board with 4 KB of working memory. They supplied parts such as the keyboard and display themselves.
takeaway: A working computer and a complete appliance were still different products for many early buyers.
visual: an exposed vintage computer board on a hobbyist's workbench
